text.p: Nasdaq stocks closed lower for the second consecutive session on Monday after hitting two new highs last week.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 7.23 points, or 0.57 percent, at 1254.57 at its unofficial close while declines led advancing issues by 2439 to 1782 on volume of about 501 million shares.

Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said the advance in Nasdaq has been due to strength in a handful of large cap OTC stocks and that negative breadth indicates secondary stocks have been left behind.
"About 50 percent of the gain in the Nasdaq this year can be attributed to Microsoft and Intel and about 20 to 30 percent to stocks like Amgen and Cisco Systems," Harrington said.
"This is indicative of a market which will eventually have a correction of some magnitude. Nasdaq is in worse shape than the index will have you believe."
Shares of Chips and Technologies fell 3-1/8 to 20-3/4 after Hambrecht & Quist said the stock was overvalued. However, it maintained a buy rating on the stock.
